tests_notes: Limits below two, exclusive limit, small primes, squares of primes skipped; workload: all 900 primes below 7000.

A.rationale: Trial division against every earlier prime is O(n·π(n)). A sieve crosses out multiples with slice assignment in C, O(n log log n), and lists the survivors in increasing order, the same list.

B.strategy: Trial division only up to sqrt(n)
B.rationale: A composite n always has a prime factor no larger than isqrt(n), so primes above it never need testing. Same primality decision, same order, far fewer divisions.

C.rationale: Sieve instead of trial division, and lru_cache returns repeated limits instantly.

C.diagnosis: Adding lru_cache changes the decorators, which must stay identical; it would also hand every caller the same mutable list. Dropped the cache, kept the sieve.
C.rationale: Marks composites in a list of booleans up to isqrt(limit) and collects the unmarked numbers in increasing order: the same primes, in O(n log log n) instead of O(n·π(n)).

notes: C first breaks a static rule (it adds @lru_cache), is told why, and its repair becomes a third win.
